Action Plan:
1. Acute dizziness/vertigo with ear buzzing and nausea:
   - Provisional diagnosis discussed: labyrinthitis.
   - Symptomatic medication prescribed (name not documented), 1 tablet three times daily for 10 days; route not documented; may be taken with or without food. Prescription sent to Lloyds Pharmacy per system.
   - Arrange in-person evaluation within the next few days to:
     • Perform otoscopic examination.
     • Check blood pressure.
     • Assess gait and basic neurological status.
   - Safety-netting: Go to the emergency department immediately if new weakness in arms or legs, sudden severe headache, or persistent/violent vomiting occurs, or if symptoms significantly worsen.
   - Patient to contact support to book the in-person appointment.
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Sudden onset dizziness/vertigo.
- History of presenting complaint:
  • Onset: About 2 hours prior to consult while making breakfast.
  • Course: Continuous since onset; room-spinning vertigo; feels unsteady when walking; able to walk.
  • Associated symptoms: Ear buzzing (tinnitus), nausea (no vomiting).
  • Denies: Hearing loss, ear pain, ear discharge, fever, recent viral illness, limb weakness.
  • Prior episode: Similar episode ~1 month ago lasting 5–10 minutes that resolved spontaneously.
- Past medical history:
  • Premature ovarian failure.
- Medications:
  • Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  • No known drug allergies.
- Social history:
  • Not discussed.

Objective:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals recorded.
- No physical examination performed.
- Investigations: None completed during consult; in-person exam planned.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute vertigo with tinnitus:
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Labyrinthitis.
   - Investigations planned: In-person assessment to include otoscopic exam, blood pressure measurement, and gait/neurological assessment.
   - Treatment planned: Symptomatic medication (name not documented), 1 tablet three times daily for 10 days; route not documented. Advice that it may be taken with or without food. Prescription sent to Lloyds Pharmacy.
   - Relevant referrals: None specified; in-person primary care evaluation arranged.
   - Safety-netting: Attend emergency department if new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, violent/persistent vomiting, or symptom escalation.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing expected elements: Vitals, full neurological exam (including HINTS if appropriate), otoscopic findings, medication name and route for prescribed vertigo treatment, specific HRT regimen (drug, dose, route, frequency), immunization status, comprehensive past medical/surgical history, social history.
- Internal conflicts: Patient reports “premature ovarian failure,” while clinician verbalized “premature hearing failure” when charting (conflict noted). Medication name for vertigo not stated; only dosing frequency and duration documented.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; brief inaudible/redacted sections where medication name was not captured.
